findings.issue_text: Spawn-context workers are `SpawnProcess` instances, so the `multiprocessing.Process` check fails to kill hung workers before replacements start, allowing concurrent flushers to process the same shards
When the shared join deadline expires, `break` skips termination of all remaining workers, potentially leaving flusher processes running after shutdown
The `wait_produce` metric uses the tag `shards` instead of `shard`, breaking consistent per-shard dashboard and alert aggregation
The added `time.sleep(0.1)` provides no synchronization because `time.sleep` was monkeypatched earlier, leaving the test scheduling-dependent
`--flusher-processes` accepts negative integers, so `-1` creates an empty process map and causes a `KeyError` during first-shard assignment instead of being rejected

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `--flusher-processes` accepts negative integers, so `-1` creates an empty process map and causes a `KeyError` during first-shard assignment instead of being rejected

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new click.Option for '--flusher-processes' with type=int and default=1, but no validation for positive values. In flusher.py, line 48 shows `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, which would use a negative value if passed (since -1 is truthy). Then line 52-53 creates `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` which with negative max_processes would result in a negative num_processes. Line 54-56 creates `self.process_to_shards_map: dict[int, list[int]] = {i: [] for i in range(self.num_processes)}` - with negative num_processes, range() produces an empty sequence, creating an empty dict. Then line 57-59 iterates over shards and tries to assign them to process_index via modulo, but with an empty process_to_shards_map, this would cause issues. The finding correctly identifies a real input validation bug.
